audit.whatIsWrong: Six of seven chart rows contradict both the packet and the page's own whys text.
audit.why: whys[0] says you trade freely before a turret exists — that is a Swain row, not Skill. whys[1] describes an explicit standoff — Skill, not Heimerdinger. whys[3] says his nest outranges everything you have — Heimerdinger, not Skill. whys[4] says his nest stops being a deterrent — Swain, not Skill. whys[6] literally calls it 'a genuine Skill check'. The packet reads Swain, Skill, Heimerdinger, Heimerdinger, Swain, Skill, Skill, and the mirror set the same shape.
audit.corrected: Rows 1, 2, 4, 5, 6 and 7 flipped to the packet in matched full/content pairs.

audit.why: Spikes are placed right: your empty-nest level 1, his 3-5 nest phase, your level 6 drain window, his first item. Demonic Ascension is a flat 120s at every rank, so the level 11 and 16 windows do not shorten — worth knowing when planning the second and third fights.

audit.whatIsWrong: wants.foe[1] says the grenade stun cancels your drain, and nothing anywhere states the range gap that defines the lane.
audit.why: Demonic Ascension is a transform with no channel — Riot's text has it lasting as long as he drains champions — so a stun does not cancel it; what it does is stop you following him out of the 650 drain radius, which ends the form for want of a target. Separately, Hextech Micro-Rockets reach 1325 and the grenade 970 against your 750 Q: that is the whole reason you cannot contest the nest, and it was never written down.
audit.corrected: Stun reframed as denial of follow-up; the 1325 / 970 / 750 range picture and the grenade's flat 11-second cooldown written in.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page says to track the grenade but never gives the number.
audit.why: CH-2 Electron Storm Grenade is 11 seconds at every rank — it does not get shorter as he levels it, so the window you wait for is the same all lane.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing warns that eating Vision of Empire feeds him nothing but feeds YOU — and that the reverse is what he wants.
audit.why: Vision of Empire grants a Soul Fragment off any champion it clips, at 5500-7500 range, so poking him inside his own nest from outside turret range is free permanent health for you. That is the counter to a lane you otherwise cannot approach.

edits.before: Both of you gain hard CC simultaneously: his CH-2 Grenade and your E root create a standoff; neither side can commit safely.
edits.after: You both get hard CC at once: his grenade stuns on a flat 11 seconds, your root returns in 12 — a standoff neither can safely open.

edits.before: His full nest plus W poke outranges every approach tool you have; farm from Q tip and wait for a grenade-down window.
edits.after: Micro-Rockets reach 1325 against your 750 Q and the nest covers the rest — farm at Q tip and wait for the grenade window.

edits.before: Land CH-2 Grenade stun on you mid-combo to cancel your drain and reset the fight on his terms
edits.after: Land the grenade stun mid-combo so you cannot follow him out of drain range and the fight resets

edits.before: Levels 3 through 5 are the hardest stretch of this lane. Three placed turrets plus W rocket poke make the entire minion wave a no-go zone for you; his nest ranges your E before you can root him, and his CH-2 Grenade peel means even a clean root gets punished on the way in. Farm from maximum Q range, never all-in, and track his grenade cooldown religiously — that is the only window you can safely approach. If he overextends to shove, angle your W from the side so turrets are not between you, then E root him away from his nest.
edits.after: Levels 3 through 5 are the hardest stretch. Micro-Rockets travel 1325 and the grenade 970 against a 750 Q, so the whole wave is his ground; the nest chips you before your 850 E can reach him. Farm at maximum Q range, never all-in, and count the grenade — a flat 11 seconds at every rank, so the window never gets shorter or longer all lane. Vision of Empire is the one free tool you have: it reaches from 5500 away and any champion it clips hands you a Soul Fragment, so poke him inside his own nest from outside turret range. If he overextends to shove, angle W from the side and root him away from the turrets.

edits.before: Level 6 flips the dynamic: Demonic Ascension drains faster than his three-turret nest can chip you down, and every second you stay inside the drain collects Soul Fragments that compound your max HP advantage. Force the fight inside his turret cluster, not outside it, so he cannot kite — root him with E to pull him close and activate R; the healing spike makes his turret focus irrelevant in a sustained drain. Post Level 6 and into items, respect his Hextech Rocketbelt dash as a grenade-dodge tool and watch for UPGRADE!!! enhanced turrets from his own R, which dramatically increase nest DPS in objective fights.
edits.after: Level 6 flips the dynamic: the drain outpaces what his nest chips off you, and each second inside it banks fragments that raise your max health permanently. The catch is the 650 radius — the form only continues while a champion is being drained, so the root and pull are not a bonus, they are what keeps your ultimate alive. Root him, pull him in, then press R; if he walks out and you cannot follow, the drain ends whether or not you were stunned. Into items, treat a Rocketbelt dash as his grenade-dodge and his escape from that radius, and expect UPGRADE!!! to enhance whichever spell he casts next in objective fights.

notes: Six of seven chart rows were wrong and each one contradicted the whys sentence printed directly beneath it — whys[6] even says 'a genuine Skill check' under a row awarded to Heimerdinger. All six flipped as one matched group to the packet and mirror. Removed the claim that the grenade stun cancels your drain: the form has no channel, and what a stun actually costs you is the ability to stay inside the 650 radius, which is the same practical warning with a true reason. Added the range picture that decides the lane (rockets 1325, grenade 970, your Q 750, your E 850) and the grenade's flat 11-second cooldown, since the page repeatedly told the player to track a cooldown it never named.
